summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive web comic about the machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars. We made two comic books that open in any browser: the Moon (19 pages) and Mars (20 pages). Each page tells the story of a real machine, has its own narration (39 audio tracks) and is built on NASA sources. Each book has 4 classroom activities. The site works in English and Russian with a one-tap switch.

The challenge asks us to tell the stories of NASA's discarded equipment. We surveyed 170 students aged 12–18: 90% would read a short comic about NASA's abandoned machines, and 60% said that stories with characters and emotions make science easier to understand. That is why we chose a comic.

It is important because humanity is returning to the Moon and heading to Mars. To understand tomorrow's missions, students should know the machines that came first.
details:
What it does. Abandoned but not Forgotten is a website with two interactive comic books: the Moon (19 pages) and Mars (20 pages). The reader turns the pages like a real book, reads the story of a real NASA machine, and presses the audio button to hear the page narrated. Each book has 4 classroom activities.

Benefits and impact. Our survey of 170 students aged 12–18 showed that 60% find science easier to understand through stories with characters and emotions. The comic gives teachers a ready resource for lessons and gives students a reason to care about the machines that came before today's missions. It works in English and Russian.

Tools. HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript in one index.html, with no frameworks or libraries. CSS 3D page-turning: a two-page spread on wide screens and one page below 760 px. Controls: buttons, click, keyboard arrows, swipe and page zoom. Web Audio API: background music fades down under the narration. Static hosting on GitHub Pages with a public repository.

Creativity. We turned NASA's catalogue of objects left on the Moon into stories with characters. Reading, listening and facts are together on one page.

Factors we considered. Privacy: no accounts, analytics or cookies; answers stay in the browser. Accuracy: every page is built on NASA sources. Honesty about AI: all illustrations are labelled "AI-generated image", and narration is noted in the audio metadata. The story, concept and choice of material are our own work.
